sections.heading: Sums as limits: the definite integral

questions.q: Explain how the definite integral $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$ is defined as a limit of Riemann sums, and write the limit expression using sigma notation.
questions.answer: $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f(x_i^*)\Delta x$, where $\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and $x_i^*$ is any sample point in the $i$-th subinterval — as $n\to\infty$ (subintervals shrink to zero width), all Riemann sum types (left, right, midpoint) converge to the same value, the exact signed area under $f$.

questions.q: Determine whether the Left Riemann Sum overestimates or underestimates $\int_0^4 x^2\,dx$, and explain why using the shape of the graph.
questions.answer: Since $f(x)=x^2$ is increasing on $[0,4]$, the left endpoint of each subinterval gives the smallest function value on that subinterval, so the Left Riemann Sum UNDERESTIMATES the true area (confirmed: $L_4=14 < \frac{64}{3}\approx21.33$).

The graph shows $f(x)=x^2$ on $[0,4]$. Use the graph to explain why the Right Riemann Sum $R_4=30$ (found earlier) overestimates the true area, and why the Left Riemann Sum $L_4=14$ underestimates it.
questions.answer: Since $f(x)=x^2$ is increasing on $[0,4]$, right-endpoint rectangles reach up to the curve's height at the RIGHT edge of each strip, so their tops poke above the curve, overestimating the area. Left-endpoint rectangles use the height at the LEFT edge (lower, since $f$ is increasing), so their tops stay below the curve, underestimating the area.

sections.heading: Comparing Riemann sums to the exact integral

questions.q: For $\int_0^4 x^2\,dx$, the exact value is $\frac{64}{3}\approx21.33$. Rank the four approximations found earlier — $L_4=14$, $R_4=30$, $M_4=21$, $T_4=22$ — from closest to farthest from the exact value, and explain which type of approximation (midpoint or trapezoidal) tends to be more accurate for a smooth curving function.
questions.answer: Distances from $21.33$: $M_4$ ($|21-21.33|=0.33$), $T_4$ ($|22-21.33|=0.67$), $L_4$ ($|14-21.33|=7.33$), $R_4$ ($|30-21.33|=8.67$). Order (closest to farthest): $M_4, T_4, L_4, R_4$. The midpoint approximation tends to be more accurate than the trapezoidal for smooth curves, because its errors are typically about half the size and opposite in sign to the trapezoidal error.
